- **A fixture is an input, and "long" is a measurement rather than an impression.** Ask production for the longest before calling a width guard proven.

**Worth reporting separately**: several of those longest names are **preferred stock and corporate NOTES** — `Apollo Global Management Inc. 7.625% Fixed-Rate Resettable Junior Subordinated Notes due 2053`, `BitMine … 9.5% Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock`. That is precisely the class of 29 instruments removed on 2026-09-21 ("I only care about equities here"); they have re-entered through a later bulk add. Not acted on — removing a ticker is the owner's call — but the screener is carrying non-equities again.

Verified after the change: **70 checks** in the spotlight suite (every cell addressed BY LABEL rather than by index, since these have been renumbered twice and an index is a statement about today's ordering), the 90-combination sweep, and the theme suite's contrast sweep re-run across all three grounds. **Proved by reverting ten times.**

The control is `spotTheme`, spotlight-scoped on purpose — when this generalises it becomes one `cardTheme` and the `.sp-*` overrides become a token. Control ids **88 against `POST_OPT_MAX` 200**. *(It generalised the same day — see below.)*

### Three grounds on EVERY card, and the 76 literals a token could not reach (2026-09-30, owner's request)
**"Only 3 colors, Dark, Light and Navy... Can you add these all promo cards."** The six grounds built on trial for the day card are removed; the three the owner kept are one shared `cardTheme` control on every template. **THE OWNER REOPENED THIS ON 2026-10-05 and a fourth ground shipped — see "A FOURTH GROUND" at the end of this section**; everything below describes the three, and holds for all four.

- **ONE CONTROL, not thirteen.** The per-template `spotTheme` / `dayTheme` selects are gone and the Ground picker sits once beside the Template picker. **Both legacy KEYS are still read, because a saved post carries them** and a stored post must not lose its ground to a rename.
  - **A LEGACY KEY BELONGS TO THE TEMPLATE IT WAS SAVED FOR.** Read unconditionally (`cardTheme || spotTheme || dayTheme`) they cross-talk: a day post carrying `dayTheme` opened on the spotlight would colour the spotlight, a ground nobody chose for it. `LEGACY_KEY` maps template to key, so `themeClass('spotlight', {dayTheme:'light'})` is dark. **Caught by the day suite's own independence checks**, which were asserting the previous behaviour and were right to fail.
- **A REMOVAL NOTHING CHECKS IS A REMOVAL THAT GETS UNDONE.** The trial block in `day-test.js` is replaced by the opposite claim: none of the six can come back — not in the markup, not through `themeOf`, not through a legacy key, and their CSS is gone.

#### THE TOKEN BLOCK WAS "MOST OF THE CARD FOR FREE" — FOR ONE CARD
The spotlight's note said so and it was true of the spotlight. Extending the grounds to all thirteen templates found what that missed: **17 distinct hex LITERALS across 76 uses**, emitted as presentation attributes and inline styles by the chart, the spark line, the verdict ladder, the bubble tints, the range bands and the fund quadrant. **A CSS variable cannot reach a literal**, and on `#f7f8fa` they run **1.1:1 to 2.6:1** — invisible rather than wrong, the failure that reads as an empty card.

- **One translation table rather than 76 decisions.** `LIGHT_INK` maps each dark value to a light one that keeps its **hue exactly** (solved in HSL, lightness alone moved). `pal.ink(hex)` is **identity on dark and navy**, so navy stays the dark palette on another ground and a future edit to a dark literal carries with no second entry to keep in step.
- **DARKENED AGAINST A FILLED TILE, NOT THE BARE ARTBOARD.** The first cut of the light values was tuned on the page at 4.68-4.99 and the sweep then caught `--faint` at **4.28:1 inside a spotlight cell**. A token safe on the ground and marginal on the furniture fails wherever a card happens to put it, so every value now clears 4.5:1 on the 0.05 ink tint. Four existing tokens moved a shade (amber, lime, orange, accent) and `--faint` with them.
- **`LADDER_LIGHT` already existed and `pal.tints` already resolved per theme** — only the spotlight used it. The other five templates printed the **dark** six-tier ladder on the light ground at 1.4-2.5:1: the words the advice board is mostly made of, unreadable. This was a routing problem, not a palette one.
- **`.avMark` was the only hardcoded colour in the STYLESHEET** (the rest are in JS), at **1.8:1 on light** — the whole avatar card a faint smudge.

#### The instrument, and three ways it was wrong first
`ground-sweep.js` walks **75 combinations — 3 grounds x 13 templates x every mode** — and measures what is DRAWN against the ground **actually behind each element**, composited up the ancestor chain. It replaced a light-only sweep that read backgrounds and borders.

- **RELATIVE LUMINANCE IS THE WRONG MEASURE FOR VISIBILITY.** The eye is far more sensitive near black, so the same perceptual step is **~38x smaller in dY on the dark ground than on the light one**: a 0.006 dY floor rejected every rail the dark card has shipped with for weeks while accepting the light ones. That is a statement about the measure, not the cards. **CIE L\* is perceptually uniform, so one floor (1.5) serves all three grounds** — the shipped rails land in a 1.65-5.67 band and an un-overridden light rail at ~0.1.
- **ONLY SHAPES THAT PAINT.** An `<svg>` root or a `<g>` inherits the UA default fill of black and paints nothing with it, so reading `fill` on every SVG node reported "1.03:1" on the dark cards. **The giveaway was that it fired on the ground that has shipped for weeks.** Also `el.className` is an `SVGAnimatedString`, so every SVG finding was labelled `[object SVGAnimatedString]`.
- **A WASH IS ATMOSPHERE, NOT INFORMATION.** The area fill under a spark line is 13% alpha by intent; a 3:1 contrast floor asks a deliberately faint tint to be a legible graphic. Low-alpha fills take the visibility rule instead.
- **It visited only each template's DEFAULT MODE**, which is how it reported twelve templates clean while the range bands, the fund quadrant and the bubble channels still carried dark literals. Four templates have a mode switch; those are the four whose other modes had never been swept.
- **AND THE INTRO'S SLIDES WERE NEVER SWEPT AT ALL — a fifth way, found 2026-10-02 while adding the How to deck.** A template with no `MODES` entry is visited on its DEFAULT slide, and the Intro's default is a cover: so its step tiles, which are most of that deck, had never been measured. Both sweeps now carry `intro` and `howto` slide entries — **93 → 102 combinations**.
- **ITS COLOUR PARSER COULD NOT READ `color-mix()` OUTPUT, AND SO REPORTED A FAULT THAT WAS NOT THERE.** `parse()` took the first three numbers of a computed colour as 0-255 channels, but `color(srgb 0.486 0.612 1 / 0.09)` — what every `color-mix()` resolves to — carries **0-1 floats**. Read as 0-255 they are essentially BLACK, so every such fill measured as vanishing into its ground. It surfaced the moment the Intro's step chips were swept, as three failures across dark, light and navy; **the arithmetic by hand says the 9% tint is ΔL\* 5.5 against its own tile, comfortably over the 1.5 floor**, and the chips have shipped looking correct for weeks. Fixed by scaling when the string begins `color(`.
  - **The tell was that it fired on a deck that has shipped unchanged for weeks**, which is the same signal that caught the relative-luminance floor: *a measure that condemns what has visibly been fine is usually the measure*.
  - **IT COST A REAL CHANGE BEFORE IT WAS DIAGNOSED.** The how-to's number chip was raised 9% → 18% to clear the phantom failure, and put back once the arithmetic said 9% was never the problem — so the chip now matches the Intro's beside it, which is what it should have been. Compute the value by hand before changing a design to satisfy an instrument.
  - **One real fault did come out of the same run and is fixed**: `.feat` was missing from the light-ground fill list that five of its siblings are on, so the Intro's step tiles — and the how-to's — were a 2.8% white tile on a white ground. The comment above that list already said *"a fill nobody can see is still a fill nobody can see"*; `.feat` had simply been missed.

#### TWO FAILURES ARE WRONG-BUT-VISIBLE, and a contrast sweep cannot see either
Both needed their own correctness check, and the second is the one that proved it:

- **The spark wash was chosen by comparing the line colour against the LITERAL `'#34d399'`.** Routing the line through the palette makes that test false on the light ground, so every spark — rising or falling — would take the **red** wash. Perfectly visible and perfectly wrong. The check is that the wash agrees in **hue** with the line above it.
- **The range card's marker ring is a cut-out authored in the ground colour**, hardcoded to OLED black, so on light it drew a **black ring**. **The revert of that fix cost nothing until a check existed** — which is exactly the "guard that was never load-bearing" this file already records twice. The claim is simply that the ring IS the ground, so that is what is measured.

Verified: **128 checks over 75 combinations, 0 failed**, plus the spotlight theme suite (26, worst contrast now 5.02 on light against 4.74) and the day suite (89). **Proved by reverting eight times**: the ink table fails 4, the verdict ladder 1, the avatar mark 1, the marker ring 2, the wash comparison 1, the tile-tuned tokens 3, the bubble tints 1, the chart line 1.
- **`size-scope-test.js`'s `NO_SCOPE` list was stale and failed at HEAD too** — it predates `day`, `spotlight` and `stock` being templates, all three of which are scope-free by design.

#### A FOURTH GROUND, which REVERSES the instruction above (2026-10-05, owner's request)
**`sky` — a light BLUE ground, offered between Light and Navy on every template.** Asked for as *"Can you use the single stock template in promo to come with a light blue theme .. just to see how it looks"*, shown as a prototype, and then committed on the owner's instruction. **It contradicts their own recorded decision — *"Only 3 colors, Dark, Light and Navy"* — which is why the reversal is written down rather than quietly absorbed**: the next reader finding four grounds under a heading that says three would otherwise read it as drift.

##### IT CARRIES TWO CLASSES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON IT COST 4KB
`cls: 'th-light th-sky'`. Light's ~27 furniture overrides exist because **a CSS variable cannot reach the 34 `rgba(255,255,255,.0x)` sites**, and on a light ground those are invisible rather than wrong — the failure that reads as an *empty* card. Sky inherits every one of them **by BEING one of them**, so it needed no second sweep of that surface; `th-sky` then redefines only the ground, the aura and the glyph. That is the bargain Navy already has with Dark, stated the other way round.

- **`classList.add` THROWS `InvalidCharacterError` ON A STRING CONTAINING A SPACE**, so a two-class ground could not be applied at all until `promo.html` split it. **Latent for the three grounds that each carry one class, and a hard failure for the first one that does not** — worth knowing before a fifth.
  - **OF THE THREE HOSTS ONLY THE STUDIO NEEDED A CHANGE, and the reason is the mechanism rather than luck.** The phone's sheet and its off-screen rasterise stage both build a class ATTRIBUTE STRING (`stage.className = 's-art sz-' + id + ' ' + d.theme`), which is space-separated by definition; `classList.add` is the one API that refuses a space. Checked rather than assumed, because a host that threw here would draw a light chart on a black card — the exact bug `themeClass` exists to stop. The studio's own `th-`-prefixed removal filter already clears both classes.
- **`themeOf` falls back to `THEMES.dark` for a key it does not know**, so a picker offering a ground the module has never heard of draws dark **silently**. That is what every ground assertion now tests, in place of the enumerations (below).

##### EVERY VALUE IS RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE GROUND, and 0.130 is why
**The ground is `#d1ecff`, the owner's own value** — *"I was thinking light blue color to be something like #d1ecff"*, which replaced the `#e0ebf9` first shipped. It is luminance **0.808** against light's **0.938**, and it is markedly bluer: **+46 of blue over red against the first value's +25**, which is what was asked for and what the earlier value was too grey to give. *(An older note here said 0.820 against 0.865 and called the gap 0.045 — that was wrong, and the error is the reason the ladder below was missed the first time.)*

Light's own tokens sit under the 4.5:1 floor on it, and further under once the **0.05 card-tile tint** (`#c7e1f3`) darkens the surface a card actually puts text on. Each is darkened a step; measured after, on that tile: **green 4.82, red 4.67, amber 4.84, flat 4.69, muted 5.23, faint 5.08**. **A value safe on the ground and marginal on the furniture fails wherever a card happens to put it.**

###### THE VERDICT LADDER WAS REUSED, AND ALL SIX ENTRIES WERE UNDER THE FLOOR
**The prototype shipped `tints: LADDER_LIGHT`, and that is the same mistake the light theme itself made on its first render** — *"Sell Immediately at 2.7:1 on white ... the card did not look broken, it looked WEAK"*. Met again, on the fourth ground, and caught only because the contrast sweep was corrected to cover it.

- **`LADDER_LIGHT` clears only ~4.52:1 on LIGHT's own card tile**, so a ground this much darker puts the whole ladder under the floor — **3.94 to 4.30** on `#d1ecff`, every one of the six. The sweep reported the single entry its fixture happened to draw (`verdict 4.43`); the other five would have failed the moment a card drew them.
- **`LADDER_SKY` darkens each entry with its channels scaled together**, so the hue is light's exactly and only the lightness moves — the `LIGHT_INK` approach rather than a second set of colours. Light's ladder is **untouched**, since it measures fine on its own ground.
- **Tuned to 4.6 on the tile, not 4.5, and the margin is the point rather than a nicety**: a ladder sitting exactly on its floor is what broke the moment the ground moved. After: **4.61 to 4.65** on the sky tile.
  - **THAT MARGIN EARNED ITS KEEP WITHIN A DAY, which is why it is recorded rather than assumed.** When the ground moved to `#d1ecff` the ladder slipped straight back onto its floor — **4.54 to 4.61** — on a luminance change of only **0.013**, nowhere near enough to put anything under it. Re-tuning cost **1 to 2 channel steps an entry**, which no eye can see, and five of the six moved. *The cheapest moment to notice a margin has been spent is while you are already editing the thing that spent it.*
- **The lesson generalises past this ground.** A new ground is not a new background colour — it is a re-measurement of every value any card draws on it, and the ones that bite are the ones reused from a neighbour because the neighbour looked close enough.

- **The aura blooms BLUE, where light's is green-and-blue.** A green wash over a blue ground reads as a stain rather than as atmosphere.
- **The chart ink map is sky's OWN** (`SKY_INK`), and that correction is the subject of the next section: light's map is tuned against a 0.938 ground and ten of its sixteen entries are under the floor on 0.808. It **spreads** `LIGHT_INK` and overrides those ten, so the six that clear both grounds still carry a future edit to light — the bargain sky has with light's furniture rules.

##### IT EXPOSED FOUR UNMAPPED DARK LITERALS, TWO ALREADY FAILING ON LIGHT
**The new ground tipped one value under its floor, and chasing it found the last four hardcoded hex paints in `cards.js`** — three `#7d8797` on axis labels (the fund quadrant's two, the bubble's one) and one `#9aa3b2` on the bubble's value caption. All four bypassed the palette entirely: the 76-literals defect, in the four places that sweep of the surface missed.

- **TWO OF THEM WERE ALREADY WRONG ON THE SHIPPED LIGHT GROUND, which is the part worth keeping.** `#9aa3b2` reads **2.42:1** on light — under even the 3:1 graphic floor — and had never been caught, because that caption is only drawn when a named dot carries a value and the swept mode has none. `#7d8797` read **3.42:1** on light: over the graphic floor, under the text one, so it passed for weeks.
- **It rode its floor across two grounds before failing.** 3.42 on light, **3.01** on the first sky ground — clearing by 0.01 — and 2.97 on `#d1ecff`. *A value scraping over its floor is indistinguishable from one that clears it, until the ground moves.*
- **The fix is `pal.axis` for the three axis labels**, which is what each theme already declares for exactly this and what six other axis labels in the module already use, and `pal.ink('#9aa3b2')` for the caption, matching the `pal.ink('#cfd6e2')` on the line above it. **All four are IDENTITY on dark, so dark cards are byte-identical**; every other ground improves: light 3.42 → 5.07 and 2.42 → 5.26, navy 4.61 → 5.51, sky 2.97 → 5.62 and 2.10 → 4.57.
- **There are now NO hardcoded hex paints left in `cards.js`**, which is a property worth grepping for rather than assuming: `fill="#......"` and `stroke="#......"` should both return nothing.

###### AND THE HOLE THEY HID IN: AN SVG `<text>`'s FILL *IS* ITS TEXT COLOUR
The sweep judged it as a **graphic at 3:1**. Its text check reads `cs.color`, which on an SVG `<text>` is the inherited CSS colour and usually paints nothing — so **text drawn the SVG way was never held to a text floor at all**, and `#7d8797` at 3.42 on light sat in the gap between the two floors. The sweep now gives a `<text>` or `<tspan>` that has its own text the text floor (4.5, or 3 where WCAG's large-text allowance applies). *A sweep with two floors will hide anything that falls between them, and the thing most likely to fall there is whatever is classified by the wrong one.*

##### AND THEN THE SHARED INK MAP: TEN OF SIXTEEN ENTRIES UNDER THE FLOOR
**`LIGHT_INK` is tuned against light's 0.938 ground and sky shares it, so on sky's card tile (`#c7e1f3`) ten of its sixteen entries land at 3.94 to 4.46** — under the 4.5:1 text floor. `SKY_INK` spreads `LIGHT_INK` and overrides those ten, each darkened with its channels scaled together so the hue is light's exactly.

- **THE SWEEP CAUGHT EXACTLY ONE OF THE TEN, and that is the point rather than a complaint about the sweep.** Only the accent is currently drawn as SVG text in a swept mode — `#2e5fe8` at **4.38:1** on a fund-quadrant label. The other nine are latent and would have surfaced one at a time, over months, as cards changed. *Fixing the one that failed and leaving nine identical cases is the same mistake as reusing a neighbour's palette because it looked close enough.*
- **LIGHT'S MAP IS UNTOUCHED, which is the call `LADDER_SKY` already made**: a shipped theme does not move to suit a new one. Darkening the shared map would have fixed sky and changed light's every chart colour, for a ground that measures fine on its own.
- **SPREAD, not restated.** The six entries that clear both grounds still carry a future edit to `LIGHT_INK` — the bargain sky already has with light's 27 furniture rules, applied to the palette.
- **A SHARED DERIVED PALETTE INHERITS THE ASSUMPTIONS OF THE GROUND IT WAS TUNED ON.** Sharing one map across two grounds is safe only while they are close in luminance, and 0.938 against 0.808 is not close. That is the general form of the lesson; sky sharing light's *furniture* is still right, because those are alpha tints that scale with whatever is behind them, where an ink value is absolute.

###### EACH FIX REVEALED THE NEXT, which is what a sweep is for
The ladder, the four literals and the ink map came out in that order, and **none of the later ones was visible until the earlier one was fixed**: the literals were hidden behind a text/graphic floor misclassification, and the ink map was hidden behind the literals, which were failing louder. Three passes of the same sweep, each clean of the previous finding and each turning up another. *A sweep that comes back clean on the first run after a change has usually not been told to look hard enough.*

##### FIVE SUITES ASSERTED "EXACTLY THREE GROUNDS" and are CORRECTED, not worked around
Every one encoded the previous instruction. **One was a blocker I missed on the first audit** (`day-test.js`), which is the argument for grepping every suite rather than the three that come to mind.

- **DERIVED, NEVER ENUMERATED.** In place of `grounds.join(',') === 'dark,light,navy'`, each now asserts the **picker and the module AGREE**: dark leads and resolves to no class, every other offered ground resolves to a non-empty one, and no two resolve to the same. That is strictly stronger — it catches the silent dark fallback, which an enumeration cannot see — and it covers a fifth ground with no edit.
- **The two sweeps already read their grounds from the live `#cardTheme` options**, so `sky` is swept across every template and mode automatically. That is what makes the contrast claim a measurement rather than an assertion: the three loops in the spotlight's own suite were the hardcoded ones and now derive too.
- **`day-test.js`'s `GONE` list is untouched and is the half that was doing the real work** — it names the six trial grounds BY NAME, so it cannot rot the way the enumeration beside it did. `sky` is not one of the six, checked rather than assumed.
- Two shot harnesses (`area-check.js`, `area-live.js`) and the contact sheet (`grounds-sheet.js`) looped over three grounds and would simply **never have looked at the new one** — on the Evolution card that loop exists to eye the area fill's strength over its own ground, which is precisely what a fourth ground changes.
- Verified: **541 checks across seven suites, 0 failed** — the ground sweep 217, the spotlight's own ground suite 34, the day card 113, the width sweep 103, the spotlight 63, note fit 7, size fit 4. The two sweeps read their grounds from the live picker, so the new one is measured across **160 ground × template × mode combinations** rather than asserted; the spotlight's own contrast sweep puts sky's worst drawn colour at **5.11:1**, against light's 5.02, navy's 5.77 and dark's 5.61. **A REVERT PROOF IS NOT WHAT HOLDS THIS DOWN, and saying so is the point** — a ground is colour, so the claim worth proving is that nothing MOVED. Five fit sweeps report ZERO overflow with the ground added: the width sweep over 120 combinations, the day card's 54, the spotlight's 90, note fit's 51 and size fit's 135, the last still at its recorded 13px tightest clearance. *(Those combination counts are larger than the ones recorded against earlier work because templates have been added since — the claim is zero overflow, not an unchanged count.)*

### A `1fr` TRACK HAS A MIN-CONTENT FLOOR, and two cards had been cut off by it (2026-09-30, owner: "the sparkles charts are not centered, they are cutting off from the right")
**Reported against the light ground and present on every ground since those cards were written.** `.spk` and `.zgrid` both set `grid-template-columns: repeat(N, 1fr)`, and **`1fr` is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`** — that auto floor is the item's MIN-CONTENT, so one long company name holds its column open, the tracks stop being equal, and their sum runs past the grid. Measured on the DARK ground before any fix:

| | tracks in a 952px body | drawn past the artboard |
|---|---|---|
| sparks, square x9 | 321 / 349 / 455 | **+142px** |
| sparks, story x12 | 375 / 464 / 536 | **+400px** |
| size, story | — | **+1,597px** (3,060px of track spill) |

- **The fix is `repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))`**, inline where the column count is known. **ONE MECHANISM, NOT TWO**: `min-width: 0` on the tile and its header fixes it equally well, and the first cut shipped both — so each revert came back clean while the other quietly held the line, which reads exactly like a guard that was never load-bearing. Three rules were deleted once the reverts said so.
- **THE SIZE CARD HAD A SECOND, INDEPENDENT FAULT the sweep found on its own**: `MAXR` is derived from `CELL`, which is `(size.h - FURNITURE) / gridRows` — **the artboard's HEIGHT and nothing else**. A disc is a square, so it is bounded by the narrower of its cell's height budget and its column's WIDTH; only height was ever considered. It shows on the story alone because that artboard is tall enough that height never binds — a four-column grid drew 326px discs in 232px tracks. **This is the only one of the four that bites when reverted (2 checks).**

#### NOTHING HERE HAD EVER MEASURED WIDTH
`size-fit`, `note-fit` and the day and spotlight sweeps all measure the body's HEIGHT against the artboard. That is the gap this lived in: a card cannot scroll sideways either, and 400px of a ranked list was simply gone. **`width-sweep.js`** walks 75 artboard x template x mode combinations and reports anything drawn past the body's content box.

- **THE CONTAINER'S OWN RECT IS THE WRONG BOX, and my first overflow check read "clean" over a card that is visibly cut off.** A grid keeps its 952px width while its TRACKS overflow, so `grid.getBoundingClientRect().width` says nothing. The honest measures are the CHILDREN's right edges against the content box, and `scrollWidth` against `clientWidth` — the same wrong-box error as reading `.s-in`'s `scrollHeight` for vertical fit, which this file already records.
- **A DELIBERATE FULL BLEED IS NOT AN OVERFLOW.** The avatar card undoes the stage's padding with negative side margins so a mark reaches every edge; it measured +128px, which is exactly the two 64px gutters — the feature working. A negative horizontal margin is that intent stated in the style, so such an element and its contents are exempt, and the artboard's own `overflow: hidden` is what makes that safe.
- **A FIXTURE IS AN INPUT, AND "LONG" IS A MEASUREMENT — met twice in one hour.** The before/after screenshot came out IDENTICAL on a fixture of nine tidy names: the bug needs a name long enough to hold its column open, and the live universe has 58 display names past 28 characters and one of 99. The same lesson the spotlight's headline step-down records.
- **A CHECK THAT PASSES SILENTLY CANNOT BE COUNTED.** The grid-spill check incremented the tally without printing, so the sweep reported 79 checks while emitting 40 lines — and the revert harness, which counts PASS/FAIL in the output, **refused the baseline as broken and was right to**: a harness that cannot count its own checks cannot tell a clean run from one that never happened. It cost two wasted runs before it was read properly.
- **THREE OF THE FOUR "FIXES" COST NOTHING WHEN REVERTED, and that is the reverts working.** `minmax(0, 1fr)` and `min-width: 0` set the same floor two different ways, so with both shipped each revert came back clean while the other quietly held the line — indistinguishable from a guard that never mattered. **Three rules were deleted**; the track-level floor is the one kept, inline where the column count is known. Only the disc-width bound bites (2 checks).

### The Disclaimer card (2026-09-30, owner's request: "create a new template for disclaimer, make it professional")
**A fourteenth template, `disclaimer`, between Announcement and Profile picture.** Two depths: **Full** (four numbered points with their wording, the standalone post) and **Short** (the four headings alone, the end of a carousel).

- **THE WORDS ARE `/terms`'s OWN, DISTILLED — not written fresh.** Four surfaces already state this position (the terms page, the card tagline, `/help` and the Intro close), and a card that softened it, or claimed something the terms do not, would be the "every feature live" error wearing legal clothes. **The test fetches the real `/terms` and asserts three phrases appear in BOTH**, so the two cannot drift into disagreeing; another check refuses the words a product like this must never print (guarantee / risk-free / profitable / safe bet).
- **FIXED TEXT, SO IT IS NOT OWNER-ONLY — that is the whole difference from Announcement.** That one is the owner's alone because it is free text in the brand's voice; there is nothing here anyone can type into, and a member who cannot post the disclaimer is the member who most needs it. There is a check that `OWNER_ONLY_TPLS` still holds `announce` and never this.
- **NO SIGNAL COLOUR ANYWHERE ON IT.** Green is up, red is down, amber is *notice this, it is old* — a disclaimer makes none of those readings, and a card shouting in amber reads as an alert rather than as the house position. Type and spacing carry it, and there is a check on the **drawn** colours.
- **NOT ONE HEX LITERAL: every value is a token**, so all three grounds resolve with no override block. That is the 76-literals lesson applied before the fact rather than after — the ground sweep passed it first time.
- **The two depths differ in DEPTH, never in claim.** Short drops the bodies and keeps all four headings; a shorter card making a weaker claim is exactly the failure worth preventing, so the test asserts the heading lists are **identical**.
- **In Short the type GROWS into the space it has** (31px → 42px on a post, 56 on a story). Four small lines floating in a frame is the story layout's own lesson, and it matters most here: a 1080px card renders about 400px wide in a feed.
- **It reads no data at all**, which the suite proves by seeding an **empty** snapshot — anything drawn, it drew from its own text. No scope pickers, so it joins `intro`/`announce`/`avatar`/`stock`/`day`/`spotlight` in `size-scope-test`'s `NO_SCOPE`.
- **An ELEVENTH hardcoded listener list in promo.html.** A control in the markup and in `CONTROL_IDS` but not in one of these saves with a post, is read by the builder, and does nothing when touched. Control ids **89 against `POST_OPT_MAX` 200**.
- Verified: **27 checks**, plus the ground sweep (137 over 81 combinations) and the width sweep (85 over 81) re-run with the new template and its two depths.
  - **A SPECULATIVE SELECTOR LIST MATCHED THE WRONG ELEMENT SILENTLY.** The fit check reached for `'.s-foot, .s-tag, .s-in > :last-child'` — and `querySelector` returns the first match in **document order, not the first selector's**, so it found `.s-tag` in the MASTHEAD and reported the kicker-to-foot gap as **a constant −88.5px on every shape and both depths**. An identical number across cases that should differ is the tell; the class was read off `chromeFoot()` rather than guessed at.

### The How to deck — training slides, one topic at a time (2026-10-02, owner's request)
**A fifteenth template, `howto`: five topics, three slides each, posted as a carousel.** The owner named the topics and their order — *"What is a theme and how to create your own theme, what is a view…, what are screens, what is advice, how to setup alerts"*. Every topic is **what it is and who can do it · the steps · what it does not do**.

#### A HOW-TO IS INSTRUCTIONS, AND THAT RAISES THE BAR ON EVERY CLAIM
This file records four occasions when copy outlived its feature — *"every feature live"*, the welcome email, *"49 columns"*, the owner-only refresh buttons. **Stale marketing disappoints; a stale STEP sends a reader to a control they do not have.** So every label in a step was read off `index.html` and `alerts.html` rather than recalled, and two guards hold it there:

- **EVERY CONTROL A STEP NAMES IN BOLD MUST EXIST IN THE PRODUCT SOURCE**, checked mechanically: the suite pulls the `<b>` spans out of the DRAWN card and fails on any string absent from those two files. That is the only check that can see this class of rot, and it is cheap. **Proved by reverting**: renaming one step's control to `New list` fails it by name.
- **WHO CAN DO IT IS ON THE COVER OF EVERY TOPIC**, because the answer genuinely differs and is not guessable — **the same screener offers a member `New personal theme` and the owner `New theme`**. That distinction is the whole reason the first topic exists, and the how-to teaches the MEMBER control. **Proved by reverting twice**: dropping the line fails 5, and pointing the step at `New theme` fails the role check *while passing the mechanical one* — a real control, simply the wrong person's.

Measured against the product rather than assumed: a **guest** can apply a screen but cannot star one (no prefs key), sees the starter views read-only, and is refused alerts outright; **writing** a screen is the owner's and a member only stars; the Advice **ladder** has been admin-only since 2026-09-26, so the topic teaches the verdict and the one rule that fired, which is what a member actually gets. The three caps the slides state were read off the constants and are worth re-reading if one moves: `MY_PORTFOLIOS_MAX` 10, `VIEWS_MAX` 10, `ALERTS_MAX` 5.

- **THE INTRO DECK'S CLOSE IS DELIBERATELY NOT REUSED.** It ends *"No account needed — try it free"*, which under a member-only how-to points at the one place the feature is not. There is a check on every slide of every topic that those words never appear. **Proved by reverting**: borrowing it fails 5.
- **The house position is asserted, not intended** — no slide may say guarantee / risk-free / profitable / safe bet / price target / stocks to buy, checked on all fifteen slides. The Advice topic states the measured truth in as many words: over twenty years *the tiers order the downside correctly and the medians are flat — it manages risk, it does not pick winners*. A training slide is the easiest place to quietly overclaim.

#### Shape
- **NUMBERED, and the numbering is TRUE** — these are steps performed in order, which is the one thing that earns a number over an icon. The box is `.feat`, the Intro's own, with the icon square carrying a digit, so it adds almost no surface for the ground sweep to re-clear; `.fi.hnum` and `.hwho` are tokens only, no literal, so all three grounds resolve with no override block (`.hwho` is added to the light fill list beside `.stmt` anyway).
- **The square trims to three steps and NAMES THE ONE IT DROPPED.** A card cannot scroll, and the last step is the one that completes the job — a deck that stops at three of four teaches the job half done. **Proved by reverting**: dropping the line fails 1.
- `Cards.howtos()` is what the studio's two pickers are built from, so a topic added in `cards.js` appears there with no second edit — the `Cards.topics()` bargain. **A TWELFTH hardcoded listener list** in promo.html; control ids **92 against `POST_OPT_MAX` 200**, counted rather than guessed.
- **A COUNT ON A TRAINING SLIDE IS READ, NEVER WRITTEN DOWN.** The screens cover said *"twenty-two of them, in six groups"* — the number this file records — and the live read says **28 in 7**: two starter screens were inserted directly after the seed, and more since. The host already hands the module its screen list for the scoped cards' Screen picker, so the slide counts that instead and omits the sentence entirely where a host passes none. A `sub` may be a function for exactly this.
- Verified: **68 checks**, including a saved post round-tripping the topic and slide and **the phone building the same card from the same module**. **Proved by reverting ten times**, every one load-bearing.
  - **A 45-COMBINATION FIT SWEEP (5 topics × 3 slides × 3 artboards): nothing overflows, tightest card 155px of headroom.**
  - **THREE METRICS IN A ROW REPORTED A CONSTANT before one measured anything.** `.s-tag` to the kicker gave **18px on every story card** — and `.s-tag` is the MASTHEAD's subtitle, the trap the Disclaimer card records, since `querySelector` returns the first match in document order. The body's bottom to the footer gave **−0px always**, because `.s-body` is a flex item that fills to it. The body's own slack gave **0 always**, because `scrollHeight` never drops below `clientHeight`. **An identical number across cases that should differ is the tell** — the honest measure is the body's height less the CONTENT block's, which varies.
  - **A `.catch(() => {})` ON A CLICK TURNS A WRONG SELECTOR INTO A SILENTLY SKIPPED STEP.** The size chips are `data-z`, not `data-size`; the swallowed click left two assertions measuring the portrait card and reporting "4 of 4" as a trim failure. A swallowed click is a test that reports on nothing.
  - **A BACKTICK IN A CSS COMMENT TOOK THE MODULE DOWN FOR THE THIRD TIME ON THIS PROJECT.** `Cards.STYLE` is itself a template literal, so `` `.feat` `` inside a comment ends the string — and **`node --check` passes**, because it is valid syntax, just an interpolation. Caught only by actually loading the module. The two new comment blocks say so in capitals above themselves.
  - **TWO OF THE REVERTS FOUND THE TEST RATHER THAN THE CODE, which is the other thing they are for.** The control-label check read `.feat h3 b` — the step's HEADING — so it never looked at `New personal theme`, which lives in the step's paragraph: the revert renaming that control to one nobody has passed the mechanical check and failed only the role one. And "changing the topic redraws the card" **still passed with the topic listener deleted**, because the helper sets the topic and THEN the slide, and the slide's listener did the redraw. Both are strengthened: every `<b>` in the step, and a check that moves the topic *alone*.

#### A fourth slide on Screens: the catalogue (2026-10-02, owner's request)
**"Naming some of the screens, as much as you can fit in."** `hnames`, third of four on that topic — what it is · how to apply one · **what is actually in there** · what it does not keep.

- **READ LIVE, like the cover's count and for the same reason.** The cover already counts them because a hardcoded "twenty-two, in six groups" was wrong the day it was written; a slide that LISTS them is the same hazard with twenty-nine chances to be wrong instead of two. Both read the same `screens` the host hands the module, so the count and the list cannot disagree. **The check is that every name on the card is in the host's own `/api/screens`** — and that it names `At a record high`, which shipped hours earlier and which no list written by hand would carry.
- **GROUPED BEFORE IT IS CAPPED, which is not merely tidier.** Stored order is `position`, so a screen appended later sits at the END whatever group it belongs to — `At a record high` is position 28 and the first group's eighth member. Capping raw order would have dropped it while the Screens menu, which collects a group by NAME, shows it eighth. The card has to agree with the menu.
- **EVERY GROUP SHOWN IS SHOWN ENTIRE.** The square's first reading put four of Technical's six under a heading that reads as the complete set, and the tail then counted Technical among the groups that were missing — *shown and missing at once*. A group is on the card whole or not at all; the degenerate case (one group bigger than the artboard) takes a partial slice of the first group and the tail then counts rather than naming.
  - **IT IS PROVED ON THE SQUARE, because that is the only artboard where the cap binds** — the other two show everything, so every membership assertion there passes whatever the grouping does. Five checks there: the cut really drops some, every group drawn is compared **member for member** against the host's own `/api/screens`, `At a record high` survives it, and the tail names what it left out. *A rule about what happens when a list is too long can only be checked where the list is too long.*
- **The caps are measured, and only the square's binds.** The 4:5 fits all 29 with **126px** to spare and the story with **425px**, so 34 is headroom against a growing catalogue; the square takes **25 in five whole groups** and says *"…and 4 more, in Earnings and Advice."* Past two dropped groups it says *"across N more groups"* — the first version listed all five and the sentence was longer than the thing it was apologising for.
- **Two newspaper columns with `break-inside: avoid` on each group**, so a heading is never orphaned from its names. Tokens only, no literal, so all three grounds resolve with no override block — the 76-literals lesson applied before the fact rather than after.

##### THE 4:5 ARTBOARD'S ID IS `portrait`, NOT `post`
`post` is only its LABEL in the studio ("Post 4:5"). Keyed on `post` the cap map never matched it and fell through to the default — **which happened to be the same number, so nothing looked wrong**. Found because the fit sweep asserted the size chip had actually MOVED rather than trusting the click: it reported `SIZE DID NOT CHANGE: wanted post, chip reads portrait`, and separately caught a later case still sitting on the story while labelled as the post. *A sweep that does not verify it changed what it meant to change is reporting one artboard's numbers under another's name.*

##### The picker's labels moved INTO the module
`promo.html` held a kind-to-label map with a bare `: kind` fallback, so a slide kind added in `cards.js` read as **`4. hnames`** in the dropdown until a second file was edited. Each slide carries its own `label` now (defaulting from `HOW_SLIDE_LABEL`, also in the module), and the studio prints it — the `basketDays` / `Cards.topics()` bargain, one owner per fact. There is a check that **every** slide names itself and that no label is just its kind.

- Verified: the deck's suite went 76 → **102 checks**. **Three of its own assertions were hardcoded to three slides and were CORRECTED, not worked around** — and the middle one is the dangerous kind:
  - `t.slides.join(',') === 'cover,hsteps,stmts'` asserted one fixed string; it now asserts the SHAPE at its ends (opens on a cover, steps second, closes on the caveats) plus an exact check that Screens is `cover,hsteps,hnames,stmts`.
  - **The house-position loop ran `for (const s of [0, 1, 2])`**, so the new slide — *the only one that prints text straight out of the database* — would have been the one slide nobody checked for a claim the terms refuse. Derived from each topic's own slide count now.
  - The fit sweep swept **45 combinations while there are 48**, the three it missed being each artboard's LAST slide on Screens. Also derived, and the count in its own message is computed rather than written.
- **The forbidden-words check SPLIT, and the line is whose claim it is.** It failed on the new slide over `Cheap, growing and profitable` — a screen NAME describing the companies a filter selects (fwd P/E under 20, revenue growth over 15%, margin over 15%), already live in the Screens menu and on `/help`, promising the reader nothing. Dropping the word outright would have put a hole in the check for the four slides that ARE copy, so the card's own words keep the full list and the data-driven names take the narrower one — guarantee / risk-free / safe bet / price target / stocks to buy, which are a claim whoever wrote them.
- **A block that inherits the slide the block above it left selected breaks the moment a check is inserted between them.** The square-trim assertions leaned on a `show('theme', 1)` a few lines up; adding the catalogue checks left them reading **0 steps** off the catalogue slide and failing over a card that was working. They select their own slide now.
- **Proved by reverting FOURTEEN times, every one load-bearing**: the template unregistered fails 32, `howTopic`/`howSlide` out of `CONTROL_IDS` 18, the Intro's "try it free" close borrowed 13, the names written down instead of read 9, the who-can-do-this line 7, a group shown in part 4, the list capped before it is grouped 3, a step renamed to a control nobody has 2, the pickers wired to no listener 2, and the owner's control, the slide's own label, the square's trim, the numbering and a forbidden claim 1 each.
  - **THE LISTENER CASE FIRST REPORTED "0 FAILED" AND HAD ABORTED AT CHECK 65** — indistinguishable from a guard that never mattered, and caught only by the harness's own `?? only N checks ran` line. With the topic listener gone the slide picker is never refilled, so `selectOption('#howSlide', '3')` asks for an option that is not there, waits 30 seconds and THROWS. The helper sets `.value` and dispatches the page's own `change` now — a missing option leaves the select empty, the card falls back, and the assertions decide rather than the wait. **The documented `page.selectOption` trap, met for the third time on this project in a week**; it then fails 2, as it should.
  - **A revert harness killed part-way leaves the file it was patching PATCHED.** The first run of this one was interrupted inside case 6 and never reached its `finally`, so `cards.js` kept the owner's `New theme` — and the next suite run reported one failure that read as a real defect in the deck. *Before diagnosing a single failure after an interrupted revert run, check the working copy against every case's replacement string.*

##### BOTH CARD SWEEPS WERE MISSING THE SLIDE, EACH IN ITS OWN WAY
Adding a fourth slide is the kind of change a sweep is supposed to pick up for free, and neither did.

- **The ground sweep DIED and said so**, which is the good failure: `selectOption` on a value the select does not carry sits in a 30-second retry and then throws, so the run ended. Its default topic is `theme`, which has three slides.
- **The width sweep SWALLOWED it and reported three more clean combinations**, which is the bad one: its mode selection carried `.catch(() => {})`, so the control never moved, the loop measured **slide 2 twice**, and the count went 102 → 105 while the catalogue slide was never swept at all. A swallowed `selectOption` is a combination that silently re-measures the previous one. It now reports the skip and does not count the case.
- **Both are pointed at the Screens topic for the how-to**, through a small `PRESET` map applied after the template is chosen — and that is better coverage than before rather than a workaround: **Screens is the only topic with four slides and it carries all four slide KINDS**, so one topic sweeps the whole deck. Clean afterwards: ground **146 checks over 105 combinations**, width **91 over 105**.
- **Patching that MODES block by script orphaned the Intro's entry into a dead object**, which would have stopped sweeping the Intro's step slides — the exact coverage hole fixed days earlier. Caught by reading the file back rather than by the run, which stayed green because a template with no entry is simply swept on its default slide.

### Two stocks on the Chart card (2026-10-02, owner's request)
**A fourth mode in the Chart template's picker, under One stock: two named companies on one plot.** The card already had a one-stock mode and a leaders mode; what was missing is the comparison `/compare` exists for on the product side, with nothing in the studio able to post it.

- **REBASED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE CARD.** Both lines are scaled to the window's first session — which the basket payload already does, so this costs no arithmetic — and that is what makes **the gap between them the relative performance**. `/compare` settled this once: two raw prices on one axis press the cheaper stock into the floor and the chart says nothing. The fixture holds the two subjects **100x apart in price** precisely so a raw plot could not pass, and the check reads the two drawn paths: they start within 1.5px of each other and then each travels 40px+ of real vertical range.
- **BLUE AND ORANGE, AND THE PAIR WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN CHOSEN BY EYE** — see the entry below, which is why. **Neither line is filled**: a fill marks a hero, and a card with two subjects has none.
- **THE AHEAD-BY FIGURE IS IN POINTS**, never as a percentage of a percentage — both numbers are already percentages from the same origin, the rule the refresh email and `/compare` both keep. The note names which stock is ahead and by how much, and still carries the price-only caveat.
- **Two refusals rather than a broken card.** One stock chosen twice is a line drawn over itself and a comparison with nothing, so it asks for a second stock; and where a symbol has no history in the window the message **names which one** — with two subjects "no stored history" does not say whose. The second picker also **defaults to a different stock**, or the card opens on its own refusal, which reads as broken rather than as a choice not yet made.
- **The moving average is the ONE STOCK card's control and moved into its own wrap for that reason**: two stocks with an average each is four lines on a card whose point is the gap between two. The scope and how-many-lines pickers stand aside, as they already did for one stock.
- **No fetch, no endpoint, no second definition.** Every universe symbol's rebased series is already in the basket the card holds, so the second line costs a lookup. `chartHistoryNeed` is untouched — it answers for the moving average, which this mode does not have.

#### "THESE TWO COLORS LOOK THE SAME" — and the check that let it through was an inequality (2026-10-02, owner, from a screenshot of AAPL against AMZN)
**It shipped as the ACCENT PAIR, periwinkle `#7c9cff` against violet `#a78bfa`, on the reasoning that green and red are spent.** That reasoning was right and incomplete: it settled which colours to avoid and never asked whether the two chosen ones could be told apart. Measured afterwards as ΔE76 in CIE Lab:

| pair | normal | deuteranopia | protanopia | light ground | worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **accent / accent-2 (shipped)** | 19 | **3** | 5 | 21 | **3** |
| cyan / pink | 91 | 25 | 24 | 83 | 24 |
| **blue `#60a5fa` / orange `#fb923c`** | 113 | 123 | 102 | 129 | **102** |
| blue / amber | 127 | 139 | 124 | 127 | 124 |

- **ΔE 3 IS THE JUST-NOTICEABLE THRESHOLD (~2.3).** So for roughly one man in twelve the two lines were not merely similar, they were **the same colour** — on a card whose entire subject is two lines. The owner reported it with normal vision at ΔE 19, which on thin lines that cross each other repeatedly is already too close.
- **BLUE AGAINST ORANGE IS THE ONE DIVERGENCE THAT SURVIVES BOTH COMMON DICHROMACIES**, which is why it is the standard pair for exactly this problem. Blue/amber measures marginally better and was passed over: **amber is the one colour in this app with a live, enforced meaning on data surfaces** (*notice this, it is old*), where orange's meaning lives in the advice ladder, which this card does not draw — and orange is already an ordinary line colour in `CHART_PALETTE`.
- **ORANGE CANNOT BE READ AS "DOWN", checked rather than assumed**: it sits **ΔE 50** from the red (`#fb7185`), which is a rose. Green and red remain refused, and the measurement independently agrees — that pair is **ΔE 10 under deuteranopia**, so the signal pair is a bad pair perceptually as well as semantically.
- Both values are already in `CHART_PALETTE` and already mapped in `LIGHT_INK`, so the ground sweep covered them from the start.

**THE LESSON IS THE CHECK, NOT THE COLOURS.** The suite asserted *"the two lines are different colours"* — an inequality, which `#7c9cff !== #a78bfa` satisfies at ΔE 3. It passed on the version the owner reported as broken. **An inequality says nothing about whether a reader can tell two tangled lines apart**, so it measures the perceptual distance now, against a floor of **ΔE 40** (clear of threshold, far below the 102 the shipped pair reaches, above the 24 adjacent-hue pairs collapse to), **asked again through both dichromacies and on all three grounds** — the light theme darkens each hue through `LIGHT_INK`, so a pair separated on black can converge on white, and the owner's report came from a light card. **Proved by reverting**: the periwinkle/violet pair fails 5, naming ΔE 19 / 3 / 5.
- **A normal-vision-only check would still have missed half of it.** 19 against a floor of 40 fails, but it is the 3 that says how bad it was.

#### TWO END TAGS AT THE SAME HEIGHT PRINT ON TOP OF EACH OTHER
`lineChart` hangs a bold `+N%` off the end of every line, and **two stocks finishing a window half a point apart is the ordinary case here** — those two numbers being the entire comparison. The tags are laid out in y order against a 26px floor now, with the stack pulled back inside the plot if it ran past the bottom; a single tag resolves to exactly the old clamp, so no other card moved.

- **It fixes the leaders card too**, which can stack eight and had the same collision — asserted there as well, since that is the mode most able to produce it.
- **Measured**: the half-point pair lands at exactly the 26px floor, and **proved by reverting** to the old clamp it draws **10.6px apart**, which is overprinted type.

- Verified: **46 checks** driving the real studio, every control changed and the card diffed — the eleven hardcoded listener lists in promo.html are a second copy of `CONTROL_IDS`, and a control missing from one saves, is read by the builder and does nothing when touched. Plus a saved post round-tripping the second stock, and the three modes beside it unchanged (one stock still draws one filled line, leaders still draws its own). **Proved by reverting thirteen times**: the branch itself fails 27, **the reported periwinkle/violet pair 5**, green and red 5, a fill on the first line 1, the same-stock guard 2, the un-named missing-history message 1, the points sentence 2, the tag de-collision 2, `chtSym2` out of the listener list 7, out of `CONTROL_IDS` 7, the moving average left showing 1, the second picker left on the same default 2, and the relabel 1.
  - **`chart-ma-studio-test.js` ASSERTED THE MARKUP AND WENT STALE** — it checked that `#chtMa` sat inside `#chtSymWrap`, which the two-stock card also shows. **Corrected, not worked around**: it asserts the control is DRAWN for one stock and hidden for each of the other three modes by name, which is strictly stronger and cannot rot the same way.
  - **THREE REVERTS FIRST REPORTED "0 FAILED" BECAUSE THE SUITE ABORTED**, which is indistinguishable from a guard that never mattered — the harness's own `?? only N checks ran` line is what caught it. A `waitForFunction` on "a line is drawn" THROWS when the card correctly refuses to draw one, and an array read of the second line throws when a revert leaves one. The wait swallows its timeout and every pair read is defensive, so all twelve reverts now run the full 42.
  - **Two fixture faults worth keeping.** A ramp spanning the whole archive is read through a 126-session window that starts partway up it, so the planned +100% came out **+45.8%** and every arithmetic expectation was a number nobody could check — the fixture is flat until well inside the window and ramps only at the end. And **an axis label is not an end tag**: the gridline `-5%` matched the first version of the tag filter, so it reported three tags on a two-line card and compared a gridline's colour against a line's. The end tags are the bold ones.

### The Intro copy went stale, and one line of it was false (2026-09-26, owner asked for a review)
**Reviewed before the first Instagram post.** All 15 slides across the four topics rendered clean against the live snapshot with no errors; **the rendering was never the problem, the words were.** The deck is now 16 slides.

- **"A guest preview with real stocks and EVERY FEATURE LIVE" was simply untrue**, and it appeared twice — on the "Five things it does" slide and on the **close, which ends all four carousels**, so it was the last line of every one. A guest gets five symbols and the screener; Ask is member-only, personal lists are member-only, and every research page redirects. The deck promised the assistant one slide earlier and devoted a whole topic to lists. It now says what a guest actually gets: *five real stocks, the whole table, every column and every verdict*. **A marketing claim is a claim, and this one was set up to disappoint on the first session.**
- **"Five research ideas were tested and four came back flat" was stale in the direction of UNDERSELLING** — which is the rarer and more annoying kind. The log carries eight framings, seven flat, and the near-miss is recorded as too small to gate a rule on. "Five tested, four flat" also implies one worked and invites the question. It reads *eight … seven* now, with "failures included", which is the actual differentiator.
- **"every score, every verdict, every rule"** dated from before the 2026-09-23 removal, when there were three composites. **Quality is the only one left**, so the opening sentence is `every verdict, every rule, every number` and the nightly line names the 1–10 Quality score and says the scale is absolute — which is what makes "a 7 means the same thing in any market" true rather than decorative.
- **The Advice cover said "four readings" and the next slide drew five rows.** Company type is the classification that picks the rulebook, not a reading, so the cover says so: *the company type picks the rulebook, four readings collapse to one word*.
- **`TIER_DEF` abbreviated two of the six words the whole slide exists to teach** — `Sell` and `Buy w/ Risk` against the product's `Sell Immediately` and `Buy with Risk`. A carousel posted beside the Advice board has to use the board's words or it teaches a vocabulary that does not match the screen. **Longer words on a fixed artboard are exactly what overflows**, so this was measured rather than eyeballed (below); the chips are a grid, so the two-line one simply sets the row height.
- **Added: a blog-and-list slide, and the close now carries the email ask.** The posts are public FIRST and the list is the convenience — the slide states them in that order, and states the terms (confirmed opt-in, one click to leave, nothing else ever) **on the slide rather than at the form**. A list nobody regrets joining is cheaper than one people report.
- Verified by `intro-fit.js`: **every slide on every artboard, 48 combinations, zero overflowing**, tightest clearance 98px, plus seven assertions on the DRAWN text (each corrected line gone, each replacement present). The overflow measurement is `.s-body`'s own, not `.s-in`'s `scrollHeight` — the Size card's lesson, since a fixed-height flex column lets its children spill without growing.

### The Size card — companies as concentric circles
**A tenth template (2026-09-20, owner's request): compare companies within a theme by size, carry other fundamentals with it, and do it as circles — "maybe two concentric circles, each representing a different measure".**

- **AREA is the encoding, never radius.** A circle of twice the radius is four times the area, so sizing by radius would quadruple the apparent gap — and in the direction people already misread a bubble chart. `r = R * sqrt(v / vmax)`, pinned by a test against arithmetic rather than by eye, and the card says so in as many words because the misreading is the default.
- **Both discs share ONE area scale whenever both are money**, which is what makes the pair worth drawing rather than decorative: the second disc's share of the first IS the ratio between the two figures. Revenue inside market cap is price-to-sales drawn rather than stated. **When revenue EXCEEDS the cap the discs simply swap** — the company trading under one times sales is the one whose circle breaks out of the ring, which is exactly what an eye should catch. Clipping it would have hidden the most interesting case.
- **A RATIO has no scale of its own**, so a margin is drawn as a share of the outer area: 50% fills half the disc. Clamped at the edge, since a margin over 100% is a data fault rather than a bigger circle, and a negative one draws no core at all.
- **The two guards are the fundamentals ranking's own, and they matter more here.** Every absolute figure is in the company's OWN reporting currency, so a single foreign reporter would dominate the picture for the wrong reason (Samsung's revenue is in won) — non-USD rows are dropped from any money comparison. And gross margin and net cash mean nothing for a lender, so banks are dropped from those.
- **A THIRD measure rides as plain text under each circle** (2026-09-20, owner's request — "a third metric like P/E or Forward P/E, only as text, just to show the valuation difference"): forward or trailing P/E, P/S, P/B, EV/EBITDA, PEG or market cap. **Deliberately not a third ring** — the card already encodes two things by area, and a multiple is a number you read one company at a time rather than a magnitude you compare at a glance; three nested circles would be decoration pretending to be data. Quieter than the two the circles carry, in the mono face, and **named once in the legend and once in the caption rather than beside every circle**, since twelve repetitions of "fwd P/E" is noise on a poster.
  - **Every multiple is the PROVIDER's own ratio, never one divided here.** Computing price-to-sales from a dollar market cap and a won revenue would produce a confident, meaningless number — the ADR trap this file records twice already.
  - **A multiple off a loss is arithmetic, not cheapness**, so a P/E at or below zero is a dash, never a negative number that would read as cheap. The same rule the Quality score and the fundamentals ranking apply.
  - **A dash means TWO different things and the caption separates them**: "1 had no meaningful multiple: a ratio off a loss is arithmetic, not cheapness. 1 does not report it." Drawing both the same and then counting one as the other is how a card quietly lies — the News column's and the data-quality page's lesson, met a third time.
- **A circle under 14px is floored AND MARKED** with a `·`, never silently enlarged: a dot drawn at its honest size is still the truth.
- **The cell is sized from the artboard's OWN height**, not the column count. A card cannot scroll — a grid too tall does not clip, it sits on top of the masthead, because `.s-body` centres its content. The first cut fixed the cell per column count and overflowed the SQUARE by 93px at four circles, the shortest artboard with the largest cells. The test sweeps 3 shapes × 5 counts × 3 inner measures and measures the artboard.
- **IT OVERFLOWED ANYWAY, and the sweep said it did not (2026-09-20).** Reported from the studio: the kicker printed on top of the brand tagline. Three things had to be got right to see it at all:
  - **`.s-in` is a fixed-height flex column, so its children overflow WITHOUT growing it.** Reading its `scrollHeight` answers "fits" while the body is spilling over the header. The honest numbers are **`.s-body`'s own overflow** and the gap between the kicker's box and the tagline's.
  - **It reproduced only in the STUDIO.** A standalone harness rendering the same card measured +4px of clearance and never collided; the studio measured −9px. Sweeping the card off-page is not the same as sweeping it where it is used, and the bug was reported against the studio.
  - **It was NOT the third measure**, which is what I assumed and said out loud — it overlapped with that switched off too. `FURNITURE` was simply set below what the card takes: measured, everything above the grid is ~395px and below it ~197px, against a reserve of 530.
  - **A single constant is a guess at variable content, which is why it now carries headroom rather than sitting on the measurement.** The caption GROWS — a sentence when circles are floored, one for a multiple off a loss, one for a figure not reported — so the tightest case is a card with both a loss-maker and an unreported figure in it, and a fixture of clean data never finds it. **`MAXR` also reserves the text height inside the cell now** (two name lines, the value, and the third measure when shown), so the disc shrinks to make room rather than the text overflowing the cell it sits in.
  - Verified by `size-fit-test.js`: **135 combinations in the studio** — 3 shapes × 5 counts × 3 third measures × 3 inner measures — asserting the kicker never reaches the tagline AND that the body never overflows at all, since a body that spills a pixel today collides on tomorrow's data. Tightest clearance 13px, zero overflowing.
- **NO BACKTICKS IN `STYLE`.** It is itself a template literal, so one inside a CSS comment ends the string and the whole module stops parsing — `ReferenceError: sub is not defined`, nowhere near the cause. Cost one debugging round.
- **A screenshot of a card is worthless without `app.css`.** The test page injected `Cards.STYLE` alone, so every token (`--green`, `--text`, the faces) was undefined, the inner disc rendered invisible and the picture said nothing about the design. The overflow measurements were unaffected; the eye check was not.
- Verified: 23 checks on the card (the area encoding against arithmetic, the shared scale, the swap, a margin filling its share, both guards, the floor marker, the words, every artboard × count × measure for overflow, and that the two discs are genuinely CONCENTRIC — same centre, whatever their sizes) and 13 on the studio wiring (the picker, the box, each control reaching the card, the industry nesting, and a **saved post restoring the template and its controls**, since a post stores controls rather than a picture).

### The Bubble card — two measures against each other, area as a third
**An eleventh template (2026-09-20, owner's request): "show the chart as bubble instead of concentric circles, or add a new template called Bubble".** Built as a new template rather than an option on Size, for a reason worth keeping:

- **A single circle per company ALREADY EXISTS** — Size with the inner measure set to none — so the option reading was very nearly a no-op. The reading worth building is the other one: a chart where **position** carries meaning. Size ranks magnitudes in a grid; Bubble asks how two measures relate and lets a third set the weight of each answer.
- **It is also not the quadrant card** (`fund` mode `quad`), which plots one FIXED pair — revenue growth against profit margin — with every dot the same size. Here both axes and the area are chosen, which makes it a different question rather than a restyling.
- **The measures are `FUND_METRICS`, exported as `Cards.bubbleMeasures()`** and used to build the studio's three pickers. Seventeen measures, one list: a copy in the markup would drift the first time one was added, and a test asserts the picker matches the catalogue exactly.
- **`plotScales` was extracted from `scatterSvg`** so the axis arithmetic — the middle-range span, the padding, the stray pinning — is not written twice. The quadrant card's own output is asserted unchanged afterwards, because a refactor that quietly rewrites a published chart is the failure to fear.
- **THE PERCENTILE TRIM DOES NOTHING AT SMALL n, which is why `fence: 'iqr'` exists.** The 2%/98% trim drops three dots at each end of the quadrant card's ~140 and behaves; at the 20 a Bubble shows, `floor(20 * 0.02)` is 0 and it trims **nothing** — so one company at 900% growth sets the axis, presses every other circle into a band a few pixels tall, and nothing is ever marked as pinned. Tukey's fence (a quartile either side, 1.5x the spread) is robust at any size and is what a small plot asks for.
- **A CIRCLE IS NOT A DOT, and two bugs came from forgetting it — both found by a screenshot, neither by an assertion.** Pinning a stray puts its CENTRE on the axis edge, which hung half of NVIDIA off the artboard: the biggest company on the card, sliced in two, *because* it was the furthest out. Centres are kept a radius inside the plot now. And labels anchored left or right of the mark — fine beside the quadrant card's 7px dots — printed "JPMorgan Chase" straight across Microsoft at 66px. A name sits **inside** its circle when the circle can hold it (the one thing a bubble can do that a scatter cannot), otherwise centred **below**; and a label that would land on one already placed is **dropped**, because an unreadable name is noise and hides the mark underneath.
- **AREA is the encoding, never radius**, checked against arithmetic rather than by eye: caps of 400/100/25 must give radii 1 : 0.5 : 0.25, where sizing by radius would give 1 : 0.25 : 0.0625. The card says so on its own face, because the misreading is the default.
- **The fundamentals guards travel with it**, and matter more here than on a ranking, because an axis is a comparison by construction: non-USD reporters are dropped from any money comparison (Samsung's revenue is in won), banks from gross margin and net cash, and loss-makers from a P/E or PEG axis. A company with **no positive area measure is drawn as a ring** at the floor size and counted in words — it still has a place on both axes, and either inventing an area or dropping it silently would misreport the screen.
- **A FOURTH measure rides as text, the Size card's own** (2026-09-20, owner: "also show as text, what you have done in the size chart"). Same catalogue (`SIZE_THIRDS`) and the same rules, now in one shared `thirdReader()` that both cards call — the provider's own ratio rather than one divided here, a **dash for a multiple off a loss** (arithmetic, not cheapness), and the **two kinds of blank counted separately**, because a company that loses money and one that does not report the figure are different facts and drawing them the same is how a card quietly lies.
  - **It rides the NAME, not every circle.** Twenty positioned, overlapping circles cannot each carry two lines of text without exactly the collisions the labelling rules exist to prevent. So it appears on the companies that are labelled — and the caption says **"Of the companies named, …"**, since a count over a subset must not be worded as a claim about the screen.
- Verified: 33 checks off-page (the area arithmetic, the guards, rings, pinning, each channel following its picker, an unknown measure key falling back, three artboards, the third measure's dash for a loss counted apart from an absent figure, money formatted currency-neutral, and the quadrant card unchanged) and 23 in the real studio, plus screenshots at true 1080px — which is what caught both drawing bugs.
  - **Two fixture traps worth keeping**: the loss-maker has to be big enough to be NAMED or its dash is never drawn and the count stays at zero; and `forwardPe: 8 + (cap % 40)` gave every company `8.0×`, a screenshot that showed the feature working and demonstrated nothing.

#### The saved-post option cap was silently eating controls
**`cleanPosts` capped a post at 40 option keys while the studio collected 63, so everything past the fortieth was dropped on save.** Found while testing Bubble's round trip; it had been true for every card whose controls sit late in `CONTROL_IDS` — **all seven of Size's, both of Intro's, and `annKick`/`annHead`/`annBody`, the Announcement card's free text, lost without a word.**

- The cap is a guard against free storage, not a budget, and **it must clear `CONTROL_IDS` with room to spare** — a template is added in promo.html and this number is nowhere near it. It is `POST_OPT_MAX` (100) now, against 63.
- **The test passed throughout, and that is the lesson.** `size-studio-test.js` saved a post, switched template, reopened it and asserted `sizeOuter === 'rev'` — **without ever moving `sizeOuter` away**, so it read a value that had never left the page. **A round-trip test that does not perturb the thing it round-trips tests nothing.** Both harnesses move every control now before reopening.

### The Evolution card — one company's filings over time (2026-10-04, owner's request)
**A seventeenth template, `evolution`, third in the studio's picker: two stacked panels on one time axis — what the business did, and what the market paid for it — plus a four-figure then→now row.** The owner's words: *"a new template called Evolution, that shows the evolution of Earning, P/E, Market cap etc for a stock using data from Edgar"*.

It reads **`sec_facts`**, so it is the first promo card sourced from the filings rather than from the snapshot or the bar archive. `GET /api/evolution?symbol=&years=` returns one trailing-twelve-month point per filed quarter — `SecFacts.ttmSeries` over `latestFilled`, the same rolling window the SEC card's own TTM row uses, so the newest point on the chart **equals** the figure on that card.

#### `sharesDiluted(t) × close(t)` UNDERSTATES NVIDIA'S PAST VALUE BY FORTY TIMES
**The decisive measurement, and the whole reason the card is shaped the way it is.** A filed share count is as-filed and **never restated for a split**; the bar archive **is** split-adjusted (`persistBars` detects a split and rewrites the symbol's history). Multiply the two together and every pre-split point is wrong by the cumulative split factor — NVDA's 4:1 of 2021 and 10:1 of 2024 compound to **40×**, which put its historical P/E at a **median of 1.0**.

- **The shipped formulation is `cap*(t) = sharesToday × close_adjusted(t)`**, which cancels splits **exactly**: an adjusted close is already quoted in today's share units. The residual error is net share issuance since *t* — slow, bounded, and directionally knowable, which is why the note says a buyback makes the earlier multiple read low.
- **Verified at the anchor, against production**: `sharesToday × today's close` beside the vendor's own market cap over twelve symbols — **8 within 2%, 11 within 3%**, worst **INTC at −5.1%**, where the diluted count and the outstanding count genuinely differ. (An earlier exploration note here claimed "±2% on 11 of 12"; that was a different sample and is corrected to what the live route actually gives.)
- **THE CARD'S LAST POINT IS PRICED AT ITS LAST FILED PERIOD END, NOT TODAY**, so comparing it with the screener's market cap measures the price move since that quarter and nothing else — measured, **NVDA +13.1% and AAPL +17.6%** at the time of writing. That is the calendar rather than the formula, and it is the first thing the next reader will mistake for a fault.
- **RECOVERING THE SPLIT FACTOR FROM THE SHARE SERIES WAS TRIED AND REFUSED.** It cannot be done cleanly: AAPL's 7:1 reads **×6.8389** and TSLA's 5:1 reads **×5.2090**, because buybacks move the count inside the same quarter and the filed dates straddle the split — and NVDA's own trail carries a junk row (564.5M → 0.5M → 582.6M, a **×1017** "jump") that any threshold would mistake for one.
- **Proved by reverting**: the naive formulation prints **$77.7B where the truth is $310.6B** on the fixture — exactly a quarter of it, the 4:1 split — and fails 5.

#### Why two panels rather than two rebased lines
Rebasing needs a positive base, and loss-makers are the ordinary case here: measured, **TSLA is loss-making in 38 of 63 filed quarters, PTON 23 of 28, CRM 19 of 42**. So the two readings get their own dollar scales, stacked — the stock page's RSI/volume pane convention — and the note says they keep their own scales.

- **A ZERO LINE ONLY WHERE THE DATA SPANS ZERO**, which is the whole difference between a revenue panel and an earnings one: profitable or not is the reading, and a line with no zero on it cannot say which side it is on. The range is the **data's own**, padded in **pixels** rather than in value — padding in value put a zero line on a revenue chart, implying a crossing that cannot happen.
- **`valueChart` is a SIBLING of `lineChart`, not a flag on it.** That one rebases every series to a percentage, which is right for comparing two stocks and useless for a dollar figure; a function that draws "everything except" is harder to follow than two small ones — the reason `sparkSVG` sits beside `chartSVG`.
- **NO P/E LINE AT ALL, and that is a measurement.** The series spikes savagely where earnings pass through nothing — CRM's maximum is **8,014** against a median of 141.8, AMZN 1,287, F 443.7 — and is simply absent for every loss-making quarter. It appears as a then→now FIGURE instead, where `trailingPe` has already refused the multiples taken off a loss.

#### The refusals, each a measured case rather than an edge one
- **Under three trailing years is a REASON, not an empty chart.** Measured: **XOM has 0 usable trailing years** (the majors use a revenue tag `secfacts.js` does not map) and a fund files no statements at all.
- **No current share count means NO VALUE PANEL, never a fallback to the filed count** — that fallback *is* the forty-fold error. **Proved by reverting**: fails 4.
- **A multiple off a loss is a dash**, through the same `trailingPe` the adjusted pages use.

**The first live reading, which is also the coverage picture**: NVDA **68 trailing years back to 2009** with a **P/E median of 37.3** (the naive formulation gave 1.0), AAPL 70, MU 64 — and **JPM stops at 2014-09-30 with 23 points**, which is the filings-coverage gap this file already records for banks and REITs rather than anything this card does. **XOM and SPY draw no card at all**: the majors' revenue tag is unmapped and a fund files no statements. The label names the window it drew, so a 2014 end is visible rather than silent.

#### All four figures share ONE "then" — the window's own ends
They were taken from the first and last non-null value of each series, which is right for a line and wrong for a row labelled then→now: the loss-making fixture's P/E had no value at the start of its window, so `firstOf` **silently reported a later, profitable quarter** — `333.5× → 89.9×`, four figures with three different "then" dates and nothing on the card saying so. Found by the suite. An absent end is an em-dash now, which is what the note already promises.

#### THE TITLE STEP CLASSES WERE SCOPED TO `.sp-in` AND DID NOTHING HERE
`t2`/`t3`/`t4` are defined under the spotlight's container only. This card is `.evo-in`, so **they were inert**: the title stayed at 66px for every name, a 32-character name and a 45-character one both drew two 67px lines, and a 99-character one drew four and **269px** of a card that did not have it. Nothing threw. **The ninth instance of this project's class-scoping trap, in the other direction** — not a loose class capturing later markup, but a class scoped to one container and reused in another, where it is simply absent. The rules are shared now, and there is a check that a long name's title is **smaller** than a short one's.

- **The chart heights are MEASURED, not chosen**, across three artboards × eight name lengths: portrait **330/232**, square **194/136**, story **545/380**, leaving 50 / 31 / 34px at each board's own worst case. A single constant is a guess at variable content, and the square was **3px over** at its worst while the story left **306px unused** in a 1920px frame.
- **THE STORY'S WORST CASE IS A *SHORT* NAME**, the opposite of the other two boards: its base title is ~84px, so 23 characters is already two lines, where 99 characters drop to t4 and take one. A 14-character probe passed it — *"long" is a measurement, not an impression*, and here so is "short".
- **The window is NOT a layout dimension** — measured, the three windows draw to the pixel the same height — so the sweep walks NAME LENGTHS instead, with one check holding that down rather than assuming it.

#### Three faults a SCREENSHOT found and no assertion did
- **The market value figure was CLIPPED** (`$310.6B → $466...`) on the one figure the card is most about. Every artboard is 1080px wide, so a quarter of the figures row is the same **227px on all three** — and the figure value therefore **cannot take a per-artboard size**. The story's 30px override clipped all four; both overrides are deleted rather than retuned, since a rule that can only ever be wrong is residue that reads as intent.
- **The zero line carried no label** on a chart whose entire point is whether the company crossed it. The gridlines are evenly spaced *values*, so zero is almost never one of them; it gets its own, dropped where it would land on a gridline's.
